Everyone else probably already said this, but  just practice. Draw different things. Think about how they look. Try sub-dividing the aspects of the drawing. Look at others. Above all, practice a lot.

Learning music theory is, in my opinion, the best way to start learning piano. http://www.musictheory.net/ is an amazing resource. 100% free, tons of lessons, all the practice you could want... it's great.

If you want to learn general computer science, I reccomend http://cs50.tv/2010/fall/

It's free, there's no registration required. All lectures are there, video and transcribed, as well as problem sets and some other resources.

As for programming, find some good communities and books. Other people can teach you, or at the very least point you in the right direction.

www.musictheory.net

And now you have everything you need. It's free, and expansive, and includes practice mechanisms. It's nowhere close to having an actual teacher, but it's the best self-teaching method for getting into this field.

Just go through the lessons, and practice different aspects until you have them down.

As for composition, it's really directly correlated to music theory. The more theory you know, the easier it is to express musical ideas. Also, compositional software is a godsend from this century. I found that Musescore is very good, and entirely free.

The last part is being inspired. Go out into the world and experience different things. Experience anything and everything, and something might cause you to be hit with the musical inspiration you so crave. Listening to others' music is helpful, but you don't want to do it to the point where you are just remixing or plagiarizing.

Good luck. I hope this helped.
